q: Fluid can exert pressure by virtue of their _____.
e: A fluid presses on a surface because of its weight. Fluid can exert pressure by virtue of their weight. Volume or shape is not this quantity.

q: Fluid represents states of matter that take the _____ of their containers.
e: A fluid has no fixed shape. It takes the shape of the container. Solids do not. Shape is the term used with Fluid represents states matter that take.
The word fluid covers liquids and gases. Fluid is either liquid (or) gas. Solid or plasma is not this quantity.

q: The pressure exerted on a body by the atmosphere due to the weight of the atmosphere is called _____.
e: Fluid pressure comes from weight. A barometer reads that pressure as the height of a mercury column. The pressure exerted on a body by the atmosphere due to the weight of the atmosphere is called atmospheric pressure. Liquid pressure or gauge pressure is not this quantity.

q: At the earth's surface the magnitude of the atmospheric pressure is about _____.
e: Atmospheric pressure is the weight of the air column on a unit area. Near the ground it is about 100 kN m⁻², not 100 N m⁻². At the earth's surface the magnitude of the atmospheric pressure is about 100 kN m^-2. Do not trade 100 kN m^-2 for 10 kN m^-2 or 1000 kN m^-2.

q: We do not normally feel the large atmospheric pressure because the pressure inside our body is almost the same as the _____ and so balance it.
e: Atmospheric pressure is the weight of the air column on a unit area. Near the ground it is about 100 kN m⁻², not 100 N m⁻². We do not normally feel the large atmospheric pressure because the pressure inside our body is almost the same as the external pressure and so balance it. Internal pressure or blood pressure is not this quantity.

q: Nose bleeding which sometimes occurs at a place of low atmospheric pressure is due to the fact that the _____ is higher than the atmospheric pressure.
e: Atmospheric pressure is the weight of the air column on a unit area. Near the ground it is about 100 kN m⁻², not 100 N m⁻². Nose bleeding which sometimes occurs at a place of low atmospheric pressure is due to the fact that the blood pressure is higher than the atmospheric pressure. Do not trade blood pressure for air pressure or water pressure.

q: The atmospheric pressure at the plains is _____ than that at the hilly regions.
e: Atmospheric pressure is the weight of the air column on a unit area. Near the ground it is about 100 kN m⁻², not 100 N m⁻². The atmospheric pressure at the plains is higher than that at the hilly regions. Do not trade higher for lower or equal.

q: The atmospheric pressure changes according to locality and _____.
e: Atmospheric pressure is the weight of the air column on a unit area. Near the ground it is about 100 kN m⁻², not 100 N m⁻². The atmospheric pressure changes according to locality and time. Temperature or humidity is not this quantity.

q: The earth is surrounded by the atmosphere up to a height of several _____.
e: The atmosphere is a deep blanket of gas with weight, so it exerts pressure. The earth is surrounded by the atmosphere up to a height of several miles. Kilometres or metres is not this quantity.

q: The atmosphere consists largely of masses of gases and has _____.
e: The atmosphere consists largely of masses of gases and has weight. Do not trade weight for no mass or zero density.
